summary: Inline text filled with the brand gradient (background-clip: text) to highlight part of a heading. Falls back to a solid color where clipping isn't supported and in forced-colors mode.
whenToUse: Highlighting a few keywords in a hero or section heading.
Short numbers or slogans on community landing pages.
whenNotToUse: Paragraphs or long text: it reduces readability.
Communicating a status (error, success): use Text tones or a Badge.

props.name: as
props.description: Inline element to render (strong/em for semantic emphasis).

props.name: tone
props.description: brand: primary → accent; text: link → accent for body text; inverse: light tints for inverse surfaces (dark heroes).

inherits: HTML attributes of the chosen element; ref to the element.
accessibility: The text remains real text: no impact on the accessible name; use as="strong" or "em" if the emphasis is semantic.
In forced-colors mode the gradient is removed and the text uses CanvasText; without background-clip support it stays a solid color with adequate contrast.
The gradient stops are tokens designed for text: still check the contrast against the actual background (use inverse on dark surfaces).
responsive: Inline: wraps with the heading; box-decoration-break: clone keeps the gradient on every line.
commonMistakes: Using tone="brand" on a dark background in the light theme: contrast is low; use inverse.
Applying it to whole paragraphs or to links (the gradient hides the link color).

examples.name: Tones
examples.title: Tones
examples.description: brand, text, and inverse on an inverse surface.

limits: The gradient requires background-clip: text and oklch interpolation; otherwise the solid color remains.
